options.description: What to pick from, as objects or as arrays of cells. Never changed.
options.name: rows

options.description: Asks with plain lines in and lines out rather than a region that redraws, for a screen reader: the question is written once, what is typed is echoed where it is typed, and nothing already written is ever moved or erased.
options.name: accessible

options.description: Whether Escape leaves the prompt to go back a step. Defaults to `false`, where Escape does nothing, as it always has.
options.name: back

options.description: The columns, as for `table()`. Inferred from the first row's keys when not given.
options.name: columns

options.description: The columns between one column and the next. Defaults to 2.
options.name: gap

options.description: Whether to draw the heading row. Defaults to `true` when any column has one.
options.name: head

options.description: How many body rows the table may take. Defaults to what the terminal has left under the question and the heading. Named for the height rather than `rows`, which is what the other list prompts call it, because here `rows` is the data -- as it is for `table()`.
options.default: what the terminal has left under the question and the heading
options.name: height

options.description: Which row starts under the cursor, by index into `rows`. Defaults to 0.
options.name: initial

options.description: Whether the cursor wraps from one end of the table to the other. Defaults to `true`.
options.name: loop

options.description: The input router to read keys through. One is built if not given.
options.name: router

options.description: What is shown once answered, for a row whose cells joined with commas are too long a line to leave behind. A `TableCellView` cell has no text to join, so the default leaves it out; a row whose view is the point of it says so here.
options.name: short

options.description: Gives the prompt up when this aborts, the way Ctrl-C does.
options.name: signal

options.description: Where keys come from. Defaults to the terminal's input.
options.name: stdin

options.description: An answer to start from: the row that is this one starts under the cursor, and beats `initial`. The row itself, compared the way a `Map` compares keys -- so it is found when `rows` is the same objects it was answered from, and dropped, leaving `initial` to decide, when it is not.
options.name: value

api.signature: function selectRow<R extends object = TableRow>(opts: SelectRowOptions<R>): Promise<R>
